notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — the crate as code is competent and aligned with workspace policy, but its self-description as a 'reference implementation' for downstream copy is several gaps wider than the disclosure section admits (query no-op, mutex contention, demo-id collision, sharing-server vs mail-server canonical confusion). The combination of 'study this as documentation' + 'this is reference quality, but…' creates a maintenance debt because every contributor who copies a gap inherits a class of issue reports.
Confidence: 75% chance of NO MISSED P0 bug. The main thing I could not verify without running probes: (a) whether the 'malformed filter deserializing as default MetadataFilterCondition' P0 (JMAP-826m.1) actually triggers in practice — I'm reasoning about it from the type shape but I did not actually attempt the request. The Filter is #[serde(untagged)] which has known surprising behavior, and Option<T> + skip_serializing_if interactions can be subtle. (b) Whether the i64-to-u64 position cast in /query is fully safe under all edge cases — I asserted it via saturating_sub but did not exhaustively verify. (c) Whether the canonical jmap-server::handle_query path actually does the re-parse-and-surface-unsupportedFilter behavior that my reasoning in JMAP-826m.9 depended on. I read the relevant code but did not trace it end-to-end with a debugger.

Least confident flags: JMAP-826m.1 (filter-shape bypass — depends on serde behavior with untagged enum + Default-friendly struct); JMAP-826m.4 (query no-op vs spec — needs an integration test to ground); JMAP-826m.34 (arg-check ordering — needs spec validation that account-resolution truly is semantically prior to method-arg parsing per RFC 8620 §3.6.2).

Uncertainty driven by: read-only review constraint. I cannot run a probe against the actual handler to confirm filter behavior. I have not exhaustively read the jmap-server::handlers module to verify the contract metadata-server depends on. I have not read draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01 §3.4.1 verbatim (only the constraint snippet quoted in the code), which limits my confidence in the spec-grounded P0s.

Would raise confidence if: I could (a) run an integration probe against the actual handlers with the malformed-filter inputs from JMAP-826m.1, (b) read RFC 8620 §3.6.2 verbatim to confirm account-resolution ordering, (c) compile and run the existing test suite to verify baseline behavior. None of these are allowed by the read-only review constraint.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — the crate's Rust idiom is mostly sound. The /review-myoss pass already absorbed the architecturally-significant idiom issues (generic-over-O when only one O supported, std::sync::Mutex across .await-fronts, JSON round-trip serialization, manual Vec::contains dedup loops). Remaining idiomatic-Rust gaps filed in this pass are six minor items: lossy as-casts in query_objects (.45), a single manual_let_else holdout (.46), stringly-typed Error types (.47), undocumented Mutex .unwrap() policy (.48), u128→u64 truncation in demo-id minter (.49), and a duplicated .expect-justification string at three call sites (.50). None are correctness bugs; the highest-priority is .47 (P1) because the stringly-typed error pattern is what a downstream contributor will copy from this 'reference implementation' touchstone. Clippy --no-deps with pedantic cast/idiom lints enabled produced exactly the same finding set, lending high confidence that no major idiom drift was missed.
Rust idiom confidence: 85% chance of no missed idiom issue. Findings filed are grounded by pedantic clippy output (.45, .46, .49 are clippy hits verbatim) and workspace AGENTS.md policy quotes (.47, .48 are policy gaps). Least confident flags: .48 (Mutex .unwrap policy) is borderline opinion-vs-policy — the workspace 'no .unwrap()' rule has an implicit poisoning exception that the source does not document. .50 is small enough it borders on bikeshedding. Uncertainty driven by: I did not run rustfmt/typos/cargo-hack feature-powerset to scope check, but those are not idiom-class tools. I also did not read jmap-mail-server's MemoryBackend in detail to confirm that the stringly-typed Error pattern is shared by the canonical sibling (if it is, the propagation rule kicks in and .47 becomes a workspace-wide finding rather than a metadata-server-specific one).

Idiom rating (2026-05-15 /review-rusty re-run): ACCEPTABLE — one new finding filed (.51, manual_let_else sibling site missed by the prior pass). Of the 13 clippy::pedantic categories that fire on this crate, 8 are workspace-wide patterns identical to the canonical jmap-mail-server: needless_pass_by_value on Arc<B> in register_*_handlers (mail-server lib.rs:148 same shape); too_many_lines on handle_*_set (every mail-server _set handler is >100 lines, often 2-7x larger than metadata-server's 230-line handle_metadata_set); .expect("derive(Serialize) on plain data is infallible") duplication (23 sites in mail-server across 9 files vs 4 sites in metadata-server); missing_errors_doc / missing_panics_doc on public handlers (mail-server is 0/many); redundant_closure on .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(|s| s.to_owned())) (memory.rs:181 in mail-server); map_unwrap_or (mail-server email.rs:1535-1536); doc_markdown bare-word identifiers (HashMap, BTreeMap, MemoryBackend etc.) (workspace-wide); MemoryError struct shape (mail-server memory.rs:473-499 same shape). Per the workspace canonical-template propagation rule, none of those belong as findings on the metadata-server epic — they need a canonical-first sweep filed against jmap-mail-server (or a /review-workspace-api pass) and then propagated to every extension-server sibling in the same pass.
Rust idiom confidence (2026-05-15 /review-rusty re-run): 90% chance of no missed metadata-server-specific idiom issue. Grounded by: (a) clippy --all-features --no-deps with -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery -W clippy::cargo on both lib and tests targets, (b) explore-agent comparison of every clippy::pedantic category against the canonical jmap-mail-server to separate metadata-server-specific drift from workspace-wide patterns, (c) targeted grep sweeps for additional patterns (let _ = discard-tuples, unwrap_or with default-shaped args, empty-string smells, new() without Default, panic!/unreachable!/todo!, double-collect chains). Least confident flag: none — .51 is the only new metadata-server-specific finding worth filing and it is grounded by a direct clippy::pedantic --tests hit at the exact location. Uncertainty driven by: I did not run cargo-hack feature-powerset (which is feature-interaction-class, not idiom-class) and I did not exhaustively read the 1162-line tests/metadata_tests.rs integration file (some test-only idiom drift may exist there but is lower-stakes than src/). The bd-review-loop iter=1 verdict=question_tool_invoked from the prior automated run is unrelated to coverage — that was a tooling failure on the agent side, not a missed-finding signal. Running out of real complaints is the correct interpretation of the low-finding-count outcome: 7 prior idiom findings (.45-.50) plus 1 new sibling-site finding (.51) is a sound idiom result for a 5647-line greenfield crate, and bikeshedding additional taste-level lints would not survive the review-comment-thread test.
Crypto/security supplement (/review-crypto-security 2026-05-15): VERDICT — LOW SECURITY EXPOSURE. The crate's intrinsic attack surface for the seven sections of /review-crypto-security is minimal:

- Section A (key material lifecycle): N/A. No keys, secrets, passwords, seeds, mnemonics. Nothing carries Zeroize or Drop-zeroing requirements. NO FINDINGS.
- Section B (side-channel hygiene): N/A. No constant-time compares needed — no MACs, no auth tags, no key bytes, no password hashes. `textMatch` is a case-insensitive substring search over public data and does not need ct_eq. NO FINDINGS.
- Section C (untrusted input at protocol boundaries): two filter walkers recurse unboundedly on attacker-controlled Filter / Value trees. The serde_json deserializer's 128-level cap + the jmap-server parse.rs documented 32-level integrator contract bound the worst case, so this is defense-in-depth at most. Filed as P3 JMAP-826m.52.
- Section D (random source quality): no security-relevant RNG. The realistic-demo-ids minter at memory.rs:388 uses SystemTime::now() nanos + AtomicU64 — explicitly demo-grade, loudly disclaimed in rustdoc, and MetadataIds are NOT credential-grade per workspace AGENTS.md 'Backend trait rule: secret-minting methods require CSPRNG' (no minted material is exploitable by guessing). NO FINDINGS.
- Section E (persistent storage of secrets): N/A. No persistence in the crate; MemoryBackend is in-memory only. NO FINDINGS.
- Section F (logging output safety): the crate has ZERO tracing/log call sites today (verified by full-tree grep). That is the right baseline. Filed P3 JMAP-826m.53 to add a log-redaction canary test before any future contributor adds tracing instrumentation that could leak isPrivate vendor content via Metadata Debug interpolation.
- Section G (algorithm and parameter choice): N/A. No cryptographic primitives used or referenced. NO FINDINGS.

Sections spent <10 minutes on: A, B, E, G. All four are genuinely N/A — there is no crypto surface in a metadata CRUD handler library. Confidence in those four is HIGH: I read the trait surface, the MemoryBackend, every #[derive] on Metadata-bearing types, and confirmed no Zeroize/secrecy/subtle/rand crate is in Cargo.toml.

Sections where I read all relevant code paths vs. only the diff: ALL of them — this was a primary review (already filed 51 prior findings) plus a security supplement, not a diff review. I read backend.rs (184 lines), helpers.rs (110), lib.rs (523), memory.rs (1811), metadata.rs (1857) — every src file in full, plus the supertrait surface in crate-jmap-server/src/handlers.rs and crate-jmap-server/src/parse.rs.

Probability I missed a P0 in this code: ~5% chance a competent third-party crypto reviewer would find a P0 issue I did not flag. Rationale: the crate's posture (library kit + transport-less + persistence-less + auth-less + no crypto primitives) is such that the structural opportunity for a P0 simply does not exist within crate boundaries. Any P0-class defect would have to live at a layer above (the consumer's HTTP transport, the consumer's persistence, the consumer's auth integration), which is by definition out of scope for this review.

The remaining 5% concern: the description-bearing error strings in /set (memory.rs:925, 935-936, helpers and metadata.rs:389/449/870 etc.) echo client-supplied field values back to the wire. If a backend Display impl or future contributor adds a description format string that interpolates Metadata.extra content (the per-user-private vendor payload), a forbidden / overQuota / alreadyExists SetError could leak that content to an unauthorised reader of the response (e.g. via shared-error-channel multi-method requests where a client requests both /get and /set on a shared mailbox in one JMAP request and the SetError surfaces an existingId belonging to another user's private record). The single-user MemoryBackend cannot demonstrate this; the disclosure already lives at memory.rs:436-444 ('the scan is account-wide, NOT per-caller') and JMAP-826m.10 captures the broader 'reference impl is a copy-paste hazard' pattern. Not filing a fifth finding because it duplicates JMAP-826m.10's coverage and is structurally subsumed by the existing 'principal_id wiring required for multi-user' disclosure.

Least confident finding: JMAP-826m.52 (filter walker recursion) — depends on the contention that 'consumer skips the 32-level depth cap' is a plausible deployment posture. If every consumer adopts the body-size + depth-cap pattern documented in jmap-server parse.rs, the finding is moot. Filed as P3 (hygiene) precisely because of that uncertainty.

No P1 'schedule a deeper pass or external review' bead is warranted: the 5% residual P0 probability is at the consumer-integration layer, not in the crate code under review here.
